text.p: Italian serie A games to be played on Sunday. Kick-off times GMT:

Should be a typical battle between two clubs whose overriding ambition this season is to avoid relegation. Piacenza look the favourites although their centre-forward Pasquale Luiso is struggling to shake off a left ankle injury and defender Mirko Conte is recovering from a car crash.

Bologna blew their chance of joining the leaders at the weekend after conceding a 90th minute equaliser against Piacenza. They should take at least a point from the Sardinians, who will be missing Uruguayan midfielder Fabian O'Neill on international duty and were held to a draw by bottom team Reggiana last weekend. Bologna will be led as usual in attack by Sweden's Kennet Andersson and Russian Igor Kolyvanov.

Internazionale need to win this one to prevent Juventus from running away at the top. Sampdoria, having posed for their Christmas charity photograph dressed as American Indian warriors, will be on the warpath after losing to Juventus at home last weekend. Inter are without Chilean striker Ivan Zamorano and Argentine midfielder Javier Zanetti. Sampdoria midfielder Christian Kerembeu is unsettled and chafing after being reprimanded for his poor performance on Sunday. To make matters worse, he also had his house burgled.

Should prove the easiest three points Juventus are likely to pick up all season. The European and world club champions are on a roll, crushing Udinese 4-1 on Wednesday to go three points clear at the top. Verona have won only one match this season and experienced midfielder Eugenio Corini has a knee injury. Juventus will be without international stars Dimas of Portugal, Yugoslav Vladimir Jugovic and Uruguayan Paolo Montero. It should not matter much, with France's Zinedine Zidane, Croat Alen Boksic and Alessandro Del Piero all available.

Likely to be a close one, with Perugia back in front of their home fans after a 4-1 thrashing at regional rivals Fiorentina. Lazio have Czech midfielder Pavel Nedved suspended while Italy striker Pierluigi Casiraghi is doubtful. Igor Protti partners Giuseppe Signori in the Lazio front-line. Good news for Lazio, less so for the player, concerns defender Jose Antonio Chamot who was not called up by Argentina and will play.

An away match but Milan should pick up three points from this one. Anything less than that will be a disappointment while the unthinkable -- defeat -- would be another huge blow. Reggiana are the only side in serie A without a win this season. Milan's Roberto Baggio is doubtful, with sciatica and defender Alessandro Costacurta is suspended but Croat Zvonimir Boban should return from injury. Reggiana's German defender Dietmar Beiersdorfer is back after suspension.

Napoli are one of the in-form teams in Italy at the moment, with fans in the city spending more on the Totocalcio pools than those of any other club. But Roma are never easy opponents in the Olympic Stadium. Napoli will be without Belgian defender Bertrand Crasson on international duty, Roma have Argentine top scorer Abel Balbo and Uruguayan attacker Carlos Fonseca absent. Argentine coach Carlos Bianchi may call up the two sons of former Italy star Bruno Conti, Andrea and Daniele.

Udinese, with German striker Oliver Bierhoff out for some time due to injury, desperately need to get their defence working. They are likely to field the same team that lost 4-1 to Juventus on Wednesday, with the exception of defender Giovanni Bia who is suspended. Fiorentina are without their three star players -- Argentine striker Daniel Batistuta, Belgian Luis Oliveira and Portugal's Rui Costa. Midfielder Anselmo Robbiati is suspended while defender Lorenzo Amoruso looks doubtful.

The match that the top clubs will be watching, mostly hoping for Vicenza to falter. Vicenza need to win to stay in touch with league leaders Juventus but that could signal the end for embattled Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti, whose team are entering serious danger in the lower reaches of the league and whose job is reportedly at risk in his first season at the club. Vicenza will be without Uruguayan marksman Marcelo Otero.
